message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (Focal Fossa) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (8 GB) |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM) – you can adjust to your needs |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (or any zone that supports RTX A6000) |
| **Project ID** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` – replace with your actual GCP project ID |
| **Service account** | `YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com` – must have `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` and `roles/compute.storageAdmin` |

> **Tip:**  
> *If you’re new to GCP, enable the Compute Engine API first (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).*  
> *Make sure the zone you pick actually offers the RTX A6000 GPU. You can check availability with `gcloud compute zones describe us-central1-a --format="json(gpuTypes)"`.*

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
SERVICE_ACCOUNT="YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create ${INSTANCE_NAME} \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=${MACHINE_TYPE} \
  --image-family=${IMAGE_FAMILY} \
  --image-project=${IMAGE_PROJECT} \
  --accelerator=type=${GPU_TYPE},count=${GPU_COUNT} \
  --service-account=${SERVICE_ACCOUNT} \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### Optional: Startup Script

Create a `startup.sh` file if you want to install NVIDIA drivers automatically:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to load the driver
reboot
```

> **Note:**  
> The `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` line tells Compute Engine to run this script after the VM boots.  
> If you prefer to install drivers manually later, omit that flag.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### Steps to use the REST API

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
   ```bash
   gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
   ```
2. Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and the service account email in the JSON above.  
3. Send the POST request (e.g., via `curl` or Postman).

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | Service account with proper IAM roles |
| ✅ | Zone supports RTX A6000 |
| ✅ | Correct machine type & GPU count |
| ✅ | Image family `ubuntu-2004-lts` |
| ✅ | Optional startup script for NVIDIA drivers |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=${ZONE}
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a fully provisioned Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an RTX A6000 GPU on Google Cloud.
